full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: Since the identical questions of law were raised in these two cases, they were heard together and are being disposed of by one judgment. 

 3. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 464 of 1994, Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the order of forfeiture of the books mentioned in paragraph 3 of the application vide Memo. No. HM (Pol-3)/book- 16/93/397 dated 8.12.93 issued by the opposite-party No. 2 and published in Bangladesh Gazette No. 52 dated 30.12.93, Part I should not be set aside. 

 4. Let us first take up Criminal Revision No. 668 of 1994. Petitioner in this case stated in his application that his books “এলমে মারেফত and “মারেফতের গোপন আলাপ” were published before hand. But these two Bengali books did not contain any objectionable materials which oppose, injure or insult the religious sentiment and fundamental faith of the followers of Islam and, as such the order of forfeiture as contained in the aforesaid notification was unjustified and unlawful. 

 5. The opposite-parties filed counter-affidavit as well as supplementary affidavit controverting the allegation made by petitioner in this case. It is further stated that in the book named at pages 12, 13, 18, 53, 69, 93, 159 and 165 there are some objectionable writings of the petitioner being the author of the books which injured and insulted the very sentiment and religious belief of the Muslims. It is further stated that in the book named “মারেফতের গোপন আলাপ” some objectionable writings were there at pages 23, 32, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48 and 49 which affected the very fundamental faith of the Muslims and thereby outraged the religious feelings of the Muslims resulting in the insult to their religious belief and sentiment. By a supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner the objectionable writings as made in those two books were mentioned and the petitioner tried to justify the writings. 

 9. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 464 of 1994 the petitioner stated that he is the author of eight books on religion which have been forfeited by the Government under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He has given the names of the eight books in his application. It is submitted that his books cannot be forfeited in view of the fact that the same do not come within the purview of section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The opposite-parties filed a counter-affidavit denying the allegations made in the application. It is their case that in those books there are certain highly objectionable, fallacious, fabricated and misleading comments and words about the Holy Quran and ideals and the fundamental belief of the Muslims. The writer-petitioner has misinterpreted the Holy Quran and ideals and tried to give new meaning and interpretation of the holy Quran injuring the fundamental belief of the Muslims and thereby insulted their religious feeling and faith. 

 16. Another book, namely “ইসলাম ধর্মের মতভেদের কারণ” was written by the same writer. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has referred to the “লেখকের কথা” at the first introduction. In the last paragraph of this page the writer has written something which appears to us that it does not injure the feelings of the Muslims. Further, it appears that with regard to this book a criminal case under section 295A of the Penal Code had been instituted by the Government against the writer. In this case the writer as accused was found guilty by the trial Court But ultimately he was acquitted by the Lower Appellate Court. Against the judgment of the lower Appellate Court, the Government had not taken any step. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has also drawn our attention to the portion of this book, namely “লেখকের কথা” in paragraph 3, but apparently we do not find anything objectionable here. 

 18. Mr. ML Bhowmick, the learned Advocate, appeared on behalf of the petitioner Dr. (Homeo) Baba Jahangir Al-Beiman Al-Shureswari, in Criminal Revision No. 668 of 1994 and Dr. Md. Abdur Rashid, the learned Advocate, appeared for the petitioner Sadaruddin Ahmed Chishty, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 464 of 1994. Arguments of both the learned Advocates are common so far as the points of law are concerned in these two cases. The learned Advocates for the petitioners have taken preliminary objection in these two matters submitting that the impugned orders have inherent defect in view of the provision of Article 55(4) of the Constitution and the Rules of Business inasmuch as the impugned notification dated 8th December, 1993 was only signed by Selina Hoque, Assistant Secretary, but not 'by order of the President.' The learned Advocates submit that every executive action shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President and since these impugned orders of forfeiture contained in the aforesaid notifications were not signed by order of the President, these impugned orders of forfeiture suffer from inherent defect. In this connection they have referred to the case of Md. Khair Ahmed vs. Bangladesh 40 DLR 359. In that case a Division Bench of this Court held that if any Government order was not issued "By order of the President", it will have inherent defect in view of the provision of the Constitution and the Rules of Business. Annexure-A of the application dated 8.12.90 is the original draft of the Gazette notification. Here it was written as আদেশ ক্রমে that means "By order". The word "President" was omitted. But in the impugned notification dated 8.12.93 it was simply issued by Selina Hoque, Assistant Secretary. 

 19. In both the cases, the Government has filed supplementary affidavits which were sworn by the Assistant Secretary, Mrs. Selina Hoque herself. In paragraph 2 of the supplementary affidavits she has stated that while passing the order and preparing the Gazette notification inadvertently and through oversight the word "President" was dropped from the original order that is, instead of "By order of the President" only "By order" was written and the word "President" was omitted. Subsequently, it was detected that in the Gazette notification "By order of the President" was not written but other portions of the Notifications were in form. In such a situation the Gazette notification remains same, but only the words “রাষ্টপতির আদেশ ক্রমে” were added in a corrected notification dated 28th of July, 1994 and another dated 11th of August, 1994. By these corrected notifications the irregularities were removed and it was stated in the corrected notifications that it would take effect from 8.12.93. 

 23. The learned Advocates for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners published their books and over those books they have got their exclusive right. Before taking away that right of publishing the books or expressing their views, the Government ought to have issued show cause notice before passing the order of forfeiture and since no prior show cause notice was issued, this has violated the principle of natural justice. The learned Deputy Attorney-General, on the other hand, submits that in a case like this the principle of natural justice is not at all attracted in view of the fact that for publishing books the petitioners are also liable to criminal prosecution. In this connection the learned Deputy Attorney General has referred to the case of Bangladesh Anjuman-e-Ahmedia vs. Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, 1993 BLD 45. In that case the book published by the petitioner was forfeited under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Instead of filing a case before this Court under section 99B of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioner preferred a Writ Petition under Article 102 of the Constitution. In that case the specific objection was raised stating that no show cause notice was issued before passing the order of forfeiture and, as such, there was violation of the principle of natural justice. It was held by their Lordships that the provisions of section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure may be invoked when the writing and publishing of a book constituted a penal offence under section 295A of the Penal Code; the order of forfeiture is a preventive action so that the author or the publisher of the book does not continue to commit the offence and under the scheme of law forfeiture is provided under the Code of Criminal Procedure and the remedy against the forfeiture having been provided under section 99B of the Code of Criminal Procedure for setting aside the order of forfeiture, the Government was not required to issue any notice to the author or publisher of the book giving him opportunity of being heard before passing the impugned order. This case is similar in view of the fact that the books in the present two cases have been forfeited by the Government under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, we hold the similar view that before forfeiting the books under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure no show cause notice was required to be issued upon the writer or publisher. According to the opinion of the Government, the offence has already been committed and, as such, the prior notice giving them to show cause will further allow the petitioners to continue with the offence in printing and publishing the objectionable books. 

 24. Mr. Rashid submits that before publishing the notification in the official Gazette under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure the Government must form its opinion as regards the basis and grounds for passing such an order. In the present case no grounds were shown in the impugned order as well as no opinion was formed by the Government in the impugned notification forfeiting the books of the present petitioners. He has further drawn our attention to section 295A of the Penal Code which provides that whoever, with deliberate and malicious intention of outraging the religious feelings of any class of the citizens of Bangladesh, by words, either spoken or written, or by visible representations, insults or attempts to insult the religion or the religious beliefs of that class, only then the Government could pass an order under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He submits that the ingredients of section 295A are totally absent in the present case and, as such, the impugned order suffers, from legal infirmity. 

 27. In this connection Mr. Rashid has referred to the case of The Woking Muslim Mission and Literary Trust, Lahore and the Civil and Military Gazette, Limited, Lahore vs. Crown 7 DLR (WP), 17 (FB) and the case of Woking Muslim Mission & Literary Trust, Lahore and the Civil & Military Gazette Ltd. Lahore vs. Crown reported in 8 DLR (FC), 110. We have gone through the aforesaid decisions of the West Pakistan High Court as well as the Federal Court. We find some fundamental difference between the facts and circumstances of the present case and those of the aforesaid two decisions. It appears that the Government was satisfied that the offence as committed in the aforesaid case was punishable under section 295A of the Penal Code. But after hearing the parties and considering the material evidence on record, the Full Bench of the West Pakistan High Court held that it was a case not under section 295A of the Penal Code, but it was a case under section 153A of the Penal Code. Against the judgment, an appeal was preferred before the Federal Court which reversed the judgment of the High Court holding that the High Court was not empowered under section 99D of the Code of Criminal Procedure to alter the charge from section 395A to section 153A of the Penal Code inasmuch as the satisfaction of the Government on the materials was on section 295A and not on section 153A of the Penal Code. Holding the above view, the Federal Court did not approve the judgment of the High Court, but in the instant case that is not the submission of the learned Advocates of the petitioners. Since there was some distinguishable features in the present case, the decision of the Federal Court as stated above will not be applicable in the facts and circumstances of this case. 

 28. Learned Deputy Attorney-General has relied on the decision reported in 1993 BLD, 45. In that case, apart from the affidavit-in-opposition, their Lordships had themselves considered the contents of the books and it was found by their Lordships as follows: 

 29. In the present case, we have gone through the impugned orders, the counter-affidavits and supplementary affidavits of the opposite-parties together with the annexures filed before the Court regarding the opinion of the religious experts. We have also gone through the books as far as practicable and we hold also the similar view as taken by their Lordships in the aforesaid decision. From the materials on record, we find that from the offensive portions of the books as discussed above the authors had the deliberate and malicious intention to outrage the religious feelings of the Muslims and thereby insult the religious belief of the Muslims of this country. 

 30. Mr. Rashid has referred to the case of the State of Uttar Pradesh vs. Lalai Singh Yadav, reported in SCC Vol. IV, 213. This case was heard and disposed of during emergency in India and the learned Judges of the Supreme Court had expressed their views on forfeiture of book under section 99A of the Code of Criminal Procedure which runs as follows: 

 31. We have gone through the aforesaid case and it appears that it was a judgment passed during emergency in India. The facts and circumstances of that case, in our view, are not identical and, as such, the same is not applicable in this case. But their Lordships' observation to the effect that the balance struck by the Government wisdom of seeing by judicial review is perfectly correct. Whatever action shall be taken by the Government under section 99A is always subject to judicial review. 

 33. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.464 of 1994 eight books were impugned and writer of all the eight books is Sadaruddin Ahmed Chishty. We have considered the materials on record as well as the contents of all the impugned eight books which were forfeited under the impugned notification dated 8.12.93. Out of eight books the following two books, namely "তফসিরে কোরানুল করিম" 6th volume and "ইসলাম ধর্মের মতভেদের কারণ" do not contain any objectionable materials for which the writer or publisher may be punished under section 295A of the Penal Code. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has failed to point out any portion of these two books which may be punishable or offensive under section 295A of the Penal Code and, as such, we hold that these two books do not come within the purview of section 99A of the Code or Criminal Procedure. But the other six books contain prejudicial materials, objectionable remarks and opinions for which, in our view, the author is liable to be punished under section 295A of the Penal Code and, as such, the impugned order of forfeiture under section 99A CrPC has been legally passed. 

 With regard to Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 464 of 1994, the Rule is made absolute in part so far it relates to two books, namely, "তফসিরে কোরানুল করিম" 6th volume and "ইসলাম ধর্মের মতভেদের কারণ" and the impugned order of forfeiture as contained in the Gazette notification dated 8.12.93, so far it relates to the aforesaid two books, is set aside. As regards other six books, the order of forfeiture as contained in impugned notification dated 8.12.93 is hereby sustained.
